definitions.explanation: A port or harbor primarily used by fishing boats for landing catches, docking, and related operations. Japan has hundreds of fishing ports along its coastline.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{漁港|ぎょこう}は{活気|かっき}がある。
examples.english: The fishing port is lively in the morning.

examples.japanese: この{漁港|ぎょこう}では{新鮮|しんせん}な{魚|さかな}が{直接|ちょくせつ}{買|か}える。
examples.english: You can buy fresh fish directly at this fishing port.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}が{近|ちか}づいているため、{漁港|ぎょこう}の{船|ふね}はすべてロープで{固定|こてい}された。
examples.english: Because a typhoon is approaching, all the boats in the fishing port have been tied down with ropes.

notes:
Composed of {漁|ぎょ} (fishing) + {港|こう} (port, harbor). A straightforward compound referring to ports whose primary function is commercial fishing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漁港|ぎょこう}の{朝市|あさいち} (fishing port morning market)
- {漁港|ぎょこう}に{水揚|みずあ}げする (to land a catch at the fishing port)
- {漁港|ぎょこう}の{食堂|しょくどう} (fishing port restaurant)
- {漁港|ぎょこう}{周辺|しゅうへん} (around the fishing port)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {港|みなと} — port, harbor; general term for any port
- {港湾|こうわん} — harbor, port facilities; more technical and administrative
- {船着|ふなつ}き{場|ば} — landing place, dock; smaller and less formal

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese {漁港|ぎょこう} are popular tourist destinations. Many have {朝市|あさいち} (morning markets) and {食堂|しょくどう} (restaurants) where visitors can eat ultra-fresh seafood. Famous fishing ports include {焼津|やいづ} (Yaizu), {銚子|ちょうし} (Choshi), and {境港|さかいみなと} (Sakaiminato).
